ordered_diagnoses: Fibrolipomatous hamartoma of the median nerve

s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive enlargement of a finger with associated neurological symptoms and limited mobility
salient_findings: Enlargement of the left middle finger since birth
Tingling at the fingertip
Limited flexion of the proximal and distal interphalangeal joints
Decreased sensation distally
Overgrowth of phalanges and surrounding soft tissue on CT scan
key_facts: The patient is a 14-year-old girl
The left middle finger has been larger than the others since birth
The finger has grown progressively over time
The patient developed tingling at the fingertip 3 months before presentation
There is limited flexion of the proximal and distal interphalangeal joints
The overlying skin is normal
There is tenderness throughout the enlargement
The temperature is normal
Sensation is decreased distally
Resistance to flexion prevents full finger flexion
Laboratory studies are unremarkable
A CT scan shows overgrowth of the proximal, middle, and distal phalanges plus surrounding soft tissue
The CT scan shows normal bone trabeculation
There are no abnormal vascular structures on the CT scan

shortlist: Fibrolipomatous hamartoma of the median nerve

shortlist.label: Macrodystrophia lipomatosa
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive enlargement of the finger with overgrowth of phalanges and surrounding soft tissue, consistent with clinical presentation

shortlist.label: Fibrolipomatous hamartoma of the median nerve
shortlist.why_kept: Association with nerve involvement and lipomatous process, matching the patient's neurological symptoms and limited mobility

shortlist.label: Lipomatosis of nerve
shortlist.why_kept: Involvement of the nerve with lipomatous changes, consistent with the patient's tingling and decreased sensation

shortlist.label: Fibrolipomatous hamartoma
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of a lipomatous process with fibromatous changes, consistent with the CT scan findings

shortlist.label: Neurilemmomatosis
shortlist.why_kept: Association with nerve sheath tumors and potential for progressive growth, although less likely given the absence of other symptoms

raw.rationale: The condition presents with progressive enlargement of the finger since birth, overgrowth of phalanges and surrounding soft tissue on CT scan, and absence of abnormal vascular structures, which are characteristic features of macrodystrophia lipomatosa

rejected.label: Fibrolipomatous hamartoma of the median nerve
rejected.why: The condition typically involves the median nerve and may not explain the diffuse overgrowth of the finger

rejected.label: Lipomatosis of nerve
rejected.why: This condition primarily affects the nerve and may not account for the bony overgrowth seen in this case

rejected.label: Fibrolipomatous hamartoma
rejected.why: Similar to fibrolipomatous hamartoma of the median nerve, it may not explain the extent of bony and soft tissue involvement

rejected.label: Neurilemmomatosis
rejected.why: This condition involves multiple neurofibromas and does not typically present with localized bony and soft tissue overgrowth
